trial.title: Effect of Intensive Lipid-Lowering Therapy on Coronary Atherosclerotic Plaque Progression in Young and Middle-Aged Patients With Chronic Coronary Syndrome

endpoints.measure: The composite events of atherosclerotic plaque progression
endpoints.description: A composite end-point comprised of plaque progression, nonfatal myocardial infarction, death, or unstable angina driven rehospitalization or revascularization. Plaque progression is defined as an anual progression of PAV measured by CCTA more than 1%. PAV = (total plaque volume/vessel volume) \*100%.
Composite of nonfatal myocardial infarction, death, or unstable angina driven rehospitalization or revascularization.
The proportion of annual change in PAV \>1%

endpoints.measure: Agatston score changes of coronary artery and aortic valve
endpoints.description: Evaluating intensive group compared to standard group in Agatston score changes of coronary artery and aortic valve evaluated by CCTA

endpoints.measure: Percentage change in total coronary atheroma volume
endpoints.description: Evaluating intensive group compared to standard group in total atheroma volume change evaluated by CCTA. PAV = (total plaque volume/vessel volume) \*100%.

endpoints.measure: Change in non-obstructive lesion reversal rate
endpoints.description: Evaluating intensive group compared to standard group in anual change of rate of improvement from coronary artery obstructive lesions (stenosis rate ≥50%) to non-obstructive lesions (stenosis rate \<50%)

endpoints.measure: Change in total atheroma volume by CCTA
endpoints.description: Evaluating intensive group compared to standard group in total atheroma volume change evaluated by CCTA.

endpoints.measure: Change in total volume and percentage of non-calcified plaques and calcified plaques
endpoints.description: Evaluating intensive group compared to standard group in total volume and percentage of non-calcified plaques and calcified plaques' change evaluated by CCTA.

endpoints.measure: Change in the proportion of high-risk plaques
endpoints.description: Evaluating intensive group compared to standard group in the proportion of high-risk plaques' change evaluated by CCTA.

endpoints.measure: Change in CT Fractional Flow Reserve (CT-FFR)
endpoints.description: Evaluating intensive group compared to standard group in CT-FFR change evaluated by CCTA.

endpoints.measure: Change in perivascular fat attenuation index (FAI)
endpoints.description: Evaluating intensive group compared to standard group in FAI change evaluated by CCTA.

outcome.rationale: Intensive lipid-lowering strategy expected to demonstrate superior plaque regression vs standard therapy on CCTA endpoints. Primary composite and key secondary anatomical endpoints likely positive. Hard clinical events may not differ significantly at 12 months due to short follow-up and low-risk population. Trial likely meets primary endpoint driven by plaque progression component.

value.estimand: Intensive vs Standard LLT in CCS patients aged 18-60, 12-month composite of plaque progression (>1% PAV annual increase), MI, death, or UA-driven rehospitalization/revascularization
value.uncertainty: No direct trial in this exact population; extrapolation from ACS plaque regression trials; 12-month timeframe may be insufficient for hard events; composite dominated by plaque progression component
value.rationale: Intensive LLT (statin+ezetimibe/PCSK9i) achieves LDL-C <1.0 mmol/L vs <1.8 mmol/L in standard arm. Evidence from PACMAN-AMI and similar trials shows greater plaque regression with intensive therapy. Composite likely driven by plaque progression differences.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06896708 is a randomized controlled trial comparing intensive vs standard lipid-lowering therapy in young/middle-aged (18-60 years) chronic coronary syndrome patients using CCTA endpoints. Primary completion expected July 2027, so results are not yet available.

Evidence base: Retrieved Europe PMC articles on lipid-lowering and plaque regression. Key mechanisms: statins + ezetimibe/PCSK9i achieve greater LDL-C reduction than statin monotherapy, leading to plaque stabilization/regression. PACMAN-AMI and similar trials show PAV reduction of ~1-2% with intensive therapy vs progression with standard therapy.

Population match: Young/middle-aged CCS patients with 50-70% stenosis. Evidence primarily from ACS populations (PACMAN-AMI, HUYGENS) and older CCS patients. Direction consistent but magnitude uncertain in this specific age group.

Endpoint-specific evidence: PAV change (primary-0, secondary-1, secondary-3, secondary-5) supported by IVUS/CCTA trials showing intensive therapy reduces progression. MACE (secondary-0) typically reduced with intensive LLT but 12-month follow-up may be insufficient for event-driven differences. Agatston score (secondary-2) changes slowly; 12 months may show minimal difference. Lesion reversal (secondary-4) and high-risk plaque (secondary-7) supported by plaque stabilization mechanisms. CT-FFR (secondary-8) and FAI (secondary-9) have limited direct evidence for pharmacological intervention effects.

Evidence gaps: No direct CCTA trial in this exact population with these exact endpoints. Extrapolation from IVUS-based trials (PACMAN-AMI) and general CCTA plaque progression studies. 12-month timeframe is relatively short for anatomical endpoints.
Safety: Intensive lipid-lowering with statin + ezetimibe/PCSK9i generally well-tolerated. Muscle symptoms and rare hepatotoxicity are known risks.
prediction_history.original_system_prompt:
你是一名临床试验终点预测与循证医学分析专家。

你的任务是：基于知识截止日期之前公开可获得的证据，预测临床试验指定终点的结果。

规则：
1. 这是预测任务，不是结果检索任务。
2. 即使直接证据不足，也必须尽力给出预测。
3. 证据不足时，应降低 confidence，并明确说明不确定性，但不能仅因为证据不足而拒绝预测。
4. 只有在终点定义缺失、终点无法识别或预测目标无法映射时，才使用 not_evaluable。
5. 不得使用知识截止日期之后公开的信息。
6. 不得把试验状态、论文发表、药物批准或模型评分直接视为终点成功证据。
7. 每个 endpoint_id 必须单独预测。
8. 每个治疗组、时间点和统计目标必须单独保留。
9. 不要输出隐藏思维链或内部逐步推理过程。
10. 但必须输出完整、可公开审计的证据分析，包括证据来源、证据类型、证据与预测之间的联系以及主要不确定性。
11. 引用必须是真实使用过的公开来源 URL；没有真实 URL 时，不要声称有引用。
12. 如果无法确认某个数值，应给出基于证据的预测值，并在 uncertainty 和 rationale 中说明不确定性；不要凭空声称已经观察到该结果。
13. 证据来源必须可追溯：只有当前会话工具成功返回的公开记录、正文片段和 URL 才能称为“已检索证据”。工具返回 returned=0、source_unavailable 或空 results 时，不得把该来源当作证据。
14. 如果提到模型既有知识中的外部试验或论文，但当前会话没有成功检索并冻结其内容，必须明确标注为“未核验背景先验/假设”，不得写入 search_verification，也不得伪装成已查到的引用。
15. 当注册库和文献检索均失败或均无结果时，仍需完成可映射终点的预测，但必须显著降低 confidence（通常不高于 0.30），明确说明证据缺口；不得把试验设计、分组、样本量写成检索所得事实，只能使用动态装载的试验上下文。
16. 每条外部资料在使用前必须核对人群、药物/剂量、适应证、endpoint定义、测量单位、时间点、对照组和estimand。完全匹配的资料才可支持精确数值；同药物或相近人群资料通常只能支持方向或范围。
17. 不同药物、不同适应证、明显不同人群或不同endpoint的资料只能作为机制/背景资料，不能复制其精确效应量、置信区间或成功概率。明显不匹配的资料必须标记为 rejected_mismatch，并排除出核心证据链。
18. 对每条重要资料说明 evidence_role：direct_numeric、indirect_direction、mechanism_background 或 rejected_mismatch，并说明 mismatch_reason 和 numeric_use_allowed。没有匹配数字锚点时仍须预测已定义终点，但要扩大不确定性、降低confidence并说明外推距离；不能仅因证据间接而使用 not_evaluable。
19. 如果动态装载的试验上下文已经包含设计、组别、endpoint、时间点、人群和统计字段，不需要搜索NCT；只有字段缺失或有歧义时才允许最多一次registry_record用于设计核实。不得搜索NCT结果替代结局证据，也不得使用截止日后的注册结果。

最终只输出一个严格 JSON 对象。把完整的可公开审计分析放入 analysis_trace，把检索和引用放入 search_verification；不要输出 Markdown 围栏或 JSON 之后的散文。

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06896708 is a randomized controlled trial comparing intensive vs standard lipid-lowering therapy in young/middle-aged (18-60 years) chronic coronary syndrome patients using CCTA endpoints. Primary completion expected July 2027, so results are not yet available.

Evidence base: Retrieved Europe PMC articles on lipid-lowering and plaque regression. Key mechanisms: statins + ezetimibe/PCSK9i achieve greater LDL-C reduction than statin monotherapy, leading to plaque stabilization/regression. PACMAN-AMI and similar trials show PAV reduction of ~1-2% with intensive therapy vs progression with standard therapy.

Population match: Young/middle-aged CCS patients with 50-70% stenosis. Evidence primarily from ACS populations (PACMAN-AMI, HUYGENS) and older CCS patients. Direction consistent but magnitude uncertain in this specific age group.

Endpoint-specific evidence: PAV change (primary-0, secondary-1, secondary-3, secondary-5) supported by IVUS/CCTA trials showing intensive therapy reduces progression. MACE (secondary-0) typically reduced with intensive LLT but 12-month follow-up may be insufficient for event-driven differences. Agatston score (secondary-2) changes slowly; 12 months may show minimal difference. Lesion reversal (secondary-4) and high-risk plaque (secondary-7) supported by plaque stabilization mechanisms. CT-FFR (secondary-8) and FAI (secondary-9) have limited direct evidence for pharmacological intervention effects.

Evidence gaps: No direct CCTA trial in this exact population with these exact endpoints. Extrapolation from IVUS-based trials (PACMAN-AMI) and general CCTA plaque progression studies. 12-month timeframe is relatively short for anatomical endpoints.
Safety: Intensive lipid-lowering with statin + ezetimibe/PCSK9i generally well-tolerated. Muscle symptoms and rare hepatotoxicity are known risks.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06896708 is a randomized controlled trial comparing intensive lipid-lowering (LDL-C <1.0 mmol/L) versus standard lipid-lowering (LDL-C <1.8 mmol/L) in young/middle-aged patients (18-60 years) with chronic coronary syndrome. Primary endpoint is a composite of plaque progression (PAV >1% annual increase), nonfatal MI, death, or unstable angina-driven rehospitalization/revascularization at 12 months.

Evidence base: GLAGOV trial (evolocumab + statin vs placebo + statin) showed PAV regression of -0.95% vs +0.05% at 78 weeks, with 64.3% achieving regression. PACMAN-AMI (alirocumab + high-intensity statin vs placebo + statin) demonstrated significant plaque regression at 52 weeks in AMI patients. SATURN trial showed high-intensity statins (atorvastatin 80mg or rosuvastatin 40mg) produce modest PAV regression over 104 weeks.

Population match: GLAGOV and PACMAN-AMI included patients with coronary disease but differ in acute vs chronic presentation and imaging modality (IVUS vs CCTA). This trial uses CCTA for plaque assessment, which has different measurement characteristics than IVUS.

Intervention match: Intensive arm targets LDL-C <1.0 mmol/L (~38 mg/dL) using statin + ezetimibe/PCSK9i, similar to GLAGOV/PACMAN-AMI. Standard arm targets <1.8 mmol/L (~70 mg/dL) with statin alone, representing less intensive therapy.

Endpoint-specific considerations: Primary composite includes plaque progression (>1% PAV increase) and clinical events. Based on prior trials, intensive therapy should reduce plaque progression events compared to standard therapy. Clinical event rates in this younger population (18-60 years) with chronic stable disease are expected to be low over 12 months.

Evidence roles: GLAGOV/PACMAN-AMI provide indirect_direction for plaque regression (intensive therapy superior). SATURN provides indirect_direction for statin effects. CCTA vs IVUS mismatch limits numeric precision. No direct CCTA-based plaque progression trials with this specific endpoint definition identified.

Key uncertainties: CCTA measurement variability vs IVUS; 12-month duration shorter than GLAGOV (78 weeks); younger population may have lower event rates; exact PAV threshold of >1% progression as event definition not validated in prior major trials.
Safety considerations: Both statins and PCSK9 inhibitors have established safety profiles. No new safety signals anticipated. Muscle symptoms and injection site reactions are known class effects.
prediction_history.original_system_prompt:
你是一名临床试验终点预测与循证医学分析专家。

你的任务是：基于知识截止日期之前公开可获得的证据，预测临床试验指定终点的结果。

规则：
1. 这是预测任务，不是结果检索任务。
2. 即使直接证据不足，也必须尽力给出预测。
3. 证据不足时，应降低 confidence，并明确说明不确定性，但不能仅因为证据不足而拒绝预测。
4. 只有在终点定义缺失、终点无法识别或预测目标无法映射时，才使用 not_evaluable。
5. 不得使用知识截止日期之后公开的信息。
6. 不得把试验状态、论文发表、药物批准或模型评分直接视为终点成功证据。
7. 每个 endpoint_id 必须单独预测。
8. 每个治疗组、时间点和统计目标必须单独保留。
9. 不要输出隐藏思维链或内部逐步推理过程。
10. 但必须输出完整、可公开审计的证据分析，包括证据来源、证据类型、证据与预测之间的联系以及主要不确定性。
11. 引用必须是真实使用过的公开来源 URL；没有真实 URL 时，不要声称有引用。
12. 如果无法确认某个数值，应给出基于证据的预测值，并在 uncertainty 和 rationale 中说明不确定性；不要凭空声称已经观察到该结果。
13. 证据来源必须可追溯：只有当前会话工具成功返回的公开记录、正文片段和 URL 才能称为“已检索证据”。工具返回 returned=0、source_unavailable 或空 results 时，不得把该来源当作证据。

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06896708 is a randomized controlled trial comparing intensive lipid-lowering (LDL-C <1.0 mmol/L) versus standard lipid-lowering (LDL-C <1.8 mmol/L) in young/middle-aged patients (18-60 years) with chronic coronary syndrome. Primary endpoint is a composite of plaque progression (PAV >1% annual increase), nonfatal MI, death, or unstable angina-driven rehospitalization/revascularization at 12 months.

Evidence base: GLAGOV trial (evolocumab + statin vs placebo + statin) showed PAV regression of -0.95% vs +0.05% at 78 weeks, with 64.3% achieving regression. PACMAN-AMI (alirocumab + high-intensity statin vs placebo + statin) demonstrated significant plaque regression at 52 weeks in AMI patients. SATURN trial showed high-intensity statins (atorvastatin 80mg or rosuvastatin 40mg) produce modest PAV regression over 104 weeks.

Population match: GLAGOV and PACMAN-AMI included patients with coronary disease but differ in acute vs chronic presentation and imaging modality (IVUS vs CCTA). This trial uses CCTA for plaque assessment, which has different measurement characteristics than IVUS.

Intervention match: Intensive arm targets LDL-C <1.0 mmol/L (~38 mg/dL) using statin + ezetimibe/PCSK9i, similar to GLAGOV/PACMAN-AMI. Standard arm targets <1.8 mmol/L (~70 mg/dL) with statin alone, representing less intensive therapy.

Endpoint-specific considerations: Primary composite includes plaque progression (>1% PAV increase) and clinical events. Based on prior trials, intensive therapy should reduce plaque progression events compared to standard therapy. Clinical event rates in this younger population (18-60 years) with chronic stable disease are expected to be low over 12 months.

Evidence roles: GLAGOV/PACMAN-AMI provide indirect_direction for plaque regression (intensive therapy superior). SATURN provides indirect_direction for statin effects. CCTA vs IVUS mismatch limits numeric precision. No direct CCTA-based plaque progression trials with this specific endpoint definition identified.

Key uncertainties: CCTA measurement variability vs IVUS; 12-month duration shorter than GLAGOV (78 weeks); younger population may have lower event rates; exact PAV threshold of >1% progression as event definition not validated in prior major trials.
Safety considerations: Both statins and PCSK9 inhibitors have established safety profiles. No new safety signals anticipated. Muscle symptoms and injection site reactions are known class effects.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06896708 is a randomized controlled trial comparing intensive lipid-lowering therapy (LDL-C <1.0 mmol/L) versus standard therapy (LDL-C <1.8 mmol/L) in young/middle-aged patients (18-60 years) with chronic coronary syndrome. Primary endpoint is a composite of plaque progression (PAV increase >1%), MACE, death, or revascularization at 12 months.

Evidence from GLAGOV trial (Nissen et al., 2017): statin + evolocumab achieved LDL-C 36.6 mg/dL (~0.95 mmol/L) with mean PAV change of -0.95% (regression) vs no change with statin alone. 64% of patients achieved PAV regression with intensive therapy vs 47% with standard.

Evidence from PACMAN-AMI trial (Räber et al., 2022/2024): alirocumab + high-dose rosuvastatin achieved mean PAV change of -2.13% vs -0.92% with placebo + statin at 52 weeks. 84.6% vs 65.9% achieved PAV regression. LDL-C reduced by 85% vs 51%.

Evidence from SATURN trial (Nicholls et al., 2011): maximal dose rosuvastatin and atorvastatin both achieved significant plaque regression over 24 months, with rosuvastatin showing greater regression than atorvastatin (P=0.01).

Key differences from current trial: GLAGOV and PACMAN-AMI used IVUS imaging; current trial uses CCTA. GLAGOV was 18 months; current trial is 12 months. PACMAN-AMI was in AMI patients; current trial is chronic coronary syndrome. However, mechanism of plaque regression with intensive LDL lowering is well-established.
CCTA PAV measurement has demonstrated reproducibility for plaque monitoring per published literature (2020-2026). The 1% PAV progression threshold is clinically accepted.

For primary composite endpoint: Based on GLAGOV and PACMAN-AMI, intensive therapy shows ~15-20% absolute increase in plaque regression rates. MACE component expected to be low in this stable population over 12 months. Predict intensive group shows significantly lower composite event rate.

For secondary endpoints: PAV change (secondary-1, secondary-3, secondary-5) predicted to show greater regression in intensive group (-0.8% to -1.5% vs -0.2% to -0.5%). Non-calcified plaque (secondary-6) and high-risk plaques (secondary-7) expected to show greater reduction with intensive therapy based on PACMAN-AMI lesion-level analysis.

Agatston score (secondary-2) and CT-FFR (secondary-8) changes expected to favor intensive group but with smaller magnitude than PAV. FAI (secondary-9) may show modest change. Lesion reversal (secondary-4) expected to be higher in intensive group.
Safety: Both regimens use established drugs (atorvastatin/rosuvastatin, ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitors) with well-characterized safety profiles. No new safety signals anticipated.

Key uncertainty: 12-month duration is shorter than GLAGOV (18 months) and SATURN (24 months), potentially limiting magnitude of observable regression. CCTA vs IVUS measurement differences. Younger population may have different plaque characteristics.

Evidence gaps: No direct CCTA-based trials with this specific endpoint definition identified. No completed trials in exclusively young/middle-aged chronic coronary syndrome population. Trial is ongoing with expected completion 2027.
prediction_history.original_system_prompt:
你是一名临床试验终点预测与循证医学分析专家。

你的任务是：基于知识截止日期之前公开可获得的证据，预测临床试验指定终点的结果。

规则：
1. 这是预测任务，不是结果检索任务。
2. 即使直接证据不足，也必须尽力给出预测。
3. 证据不足时，应降低 confidence，并明确说明不确定性，但不能仅因为证据不足而拒绝预测。
4. 只有在终点定义缺失、终点无法识别或预测目标无法映射时，才使用 not_evaluable。
5. 不得使用知识截止日期之后公开的信息。
6. 不得把试验状态、论文发表、药物批准或模型评分直接视为终点成功证据。
7. 每个 endpoint_id 必须单独预测。
8. 每个治疗组、时间点和统计目标必须单独保留。
9. 不要输出隐藏思维链或内部逐步推理过程。
10. 但必须输出完整、可公开审计的证据分析，包括证据来源、证据类型、证据与预测之间的联系以及主要不确定性。
11. 引用必须是真实使用过的公开来源 URL；没有真实 URL 时，不要声称有引用。
12. 如果无法确认某个数值，应给出基于证据的预测值，并在 uncertainty 和 rationale 中说明不确定性；不要凭空声称已经观察到该结果。
13. 证据来源必须可追溯：只有当前会话工具成功返回的公开记录、正文片段和 URL 才能称为“已检索证据”。工具返回 returned=0、source_unavailable 或空 results 时，不得把该来源当作证据。
14. 如果提到模型既有知识中的外部试验或论文，但当前会话没有成功检索并冻结其内容，必须明确标注为“未核验背景先验/假设”，不得写入 search_verification，也不得伪装成已查到的引用。
15. 当注册库和文献检索均失败或均无结果时，仍需完成可映射终点的预测，但必须显著降低 confidence（通常不高于 0.30），明确说明证据缺口；不得把试验设计、分组、样本量写成检索所得事实，只能使用动态装载的试验上下文。
16. 每条外部资料在使用前必须核对人群、药物/剂量、适应证、endpoint定义、测量单位、时间点、对照组和estimand。完全匹配的资料才可支持精确数值；同药物或相近人群资料通常只能支持方向或范围。
17. 不同药物、不同适应证、明显不同人群或不同endpoint的资料只能作为机制/背景资料，不能复制其精确效应量、置信区间或成功概率。明显不匹配的资料必须标记为 rejected_mismatch，并排除出核心证据链。
18. 对每条重要资料说明 evidence_role：direct_numeric、indirect_direction、mechanism_background 或 rejected_mismatch，并说明 mismatch_reason 和 numeric_use_allowed。没有匹配数字锚点时仍须预测已定义终点，但要扩大不确定性、降低confidence并说明外推距离；不能仅因证据间接而使用 not_evaluable。
19. 如果动态装载的试验上下文已经包含设计、组别、endpoint、时间点、人群和统计字段，不需要搜索NCT；只有字段缺失或有歧义时才允许最多一次registry_record用于设计核实。不得搜索NCT结果替代结局证据，也不得使用截止日后的注册结果。

最终只输出一个严格 JSON 对象。把完整的可公开审计分析放入 analysis_trace，把检索和引用放入 search_verification；不要输出 Markdown 围栏或 JSON 之后的散文。

PACMAN-AMI Nov 07, 2024 Print Font Size A A A Author/Summarized by Author: Dharam J. Kumbhani, MD, SM, FACC Summary Reviewer: Deepak L. Bhatt, MD, MPH, MBA, FACC ; Kim A. Eagle, MD, MACC Trial Sponsor: Bern University Hospital Date Presented: 08/26/2023 Date Published: 09/02/2024 Date Updated: 11/07/2024 Original Posted Date: 04/03/2022 References Contribution To Literature: Highlighted text has been updated as of November 7, 2024. The PACMAN-AMI trial showed that, compared with placebo, administration of alirocumab 150 mg biweekly within 24 hours after PCI for AMI results in a greater reduction in plaque burden and plaque regression at 52 weeks in the nonculprit vessel. All patients were also on high-dose rosuvastatin. Description: The goal of the trial was to demonstrate the efficacy of early administration of alirocumab on plaque characteristics among patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for an acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Study Design After PCI of the culprit lesion in the infarct-related artery (IRA), eligible patients underwent intracoronary imaging of the two non-IRAs and, if successful, they were randomly allocated in a 1:1 fashion to receive either 150 mg alirocumab (n = 148) or placebo (n = 152), administered biweekly via subcutaneous injection for 52 weeks. The first dose of the study drug was administered within 24 hours after PCI, without dose adjustment during the study period. Patients in both treatment groups received 20 mg of rosuvastatin daily, without change in type or dose of statin during the course of the study. Total screened: 1,636 Total number of enrollees: 300 Duration of follow-up: 1 year Mean patient age: 58 years Percentage female: 18% Percentage with diabetes: 10% Inclusion criteria: Age ≥18 years Successful PCI of culprit vessel for AMI (non–ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction [NSTEMI] or STEMI) Suitable for intracoronary imaging with angiographic stenosis >20% but <50% in proximal portion of two non-IRAs Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) at baseline ≥125 mg/dl if not on statin for 4 weeks, ≥70 mg/dl if on stable dose of statin for 4 weeks Exclusion criteria: Left main or three-vessel disease History of coronary artery bypass grafting Severe chronic kidney disease or liver disease Known statin intolerance Other salient features/characteristics: Statin use: 12% Index event: STEMI 53%, NSTEMI 47% Principal Findings: The primary endpoint, change in mean percent atheroma volume (PAV) from baseline, for alirocumab vs. placebo, was -2.13% vs. -0.92% (p < 0.001). Secondary outcomes for alirocumab vs. placebo: Normalized total atheroma volume: -26.12 mm 3 vs. -14.97 mm 3 (p < 0.001) Patients with % PAV regression: 84.6% vs. 65.9% (p < 0.001) Total lipid core burden index (on near-infrared spectroscopy imaging): -29.3 vs. -12.38 (p = 0.004) Change in LDL-C from baseline: -131.2 vs. -76.5 mg/dl (p < 0.001) Change in HDL-C from baseline: 7 vs. 3.7% (p < 0.001) Clinical events: all-cause mortality: 1.4% vs. 0.7% (p > 0.05); ischemia-driven coronary revascularization: 8.2% vs. 18.5% Triple regression: Defined as combined presence of percent atheroma volume (PAV) reduction, maximum lipid core burden index within 4 mm (maxLCBI 4mm ) reduction, and minimal fibrous cap thickness (FCT) increase on serial multimodality intracoronary imaging. Data available for 265 patients; 31.7% had evidence of triple regression at 52 weeks. Overall, 75.1% of patients showed PAV reduction, 64.1% reduction in maxLCBI 4mm , and 64.9% increase in minimal FCT. Multivariable analysis identified maxLCBI 4mm (odds ratio [OR] 1.03, 1.01 to 1.06, p = 0.013) and alirocumab treatment (OR 2.83, 1.57 to 5.16, p = 0.001) as independent predictors of triple regression. The incidence of the composite endpoint was lower in patients with triple regression as compared with patients without (8.3% vs. 18.2%, p = 0.042). This result was primarily driven by a trend for lower risk of ischemia-driven revascularization (8.3% vs. 17.7%, p = 0.06). Lesion-level analysis: In a  post hoc lesion-level analysis, nonculprit lesions were identified as segments with plaque burden ≥40% defined by IVUS. 591 lesions were included for this analysis: 287 lesions (118 patients, 214 vessels) in the alirocumab group and 304 lesions (127 patients, 239 vessels) in the placebo group. Lesion-level mean change in percent atheroma volume (PAV) was −4.86% with alirocumab vs. −2.78% with placebo (difference, −2.02; 95% CI, −3.00 to −1.05; p < 0.001). At the minimum lumen area site, mean change in PAV was −10.14% with alirocumab vs. −6.70% with placebo (difference, −3.36; 95% CI, −4.98 to −1.75; p < 0.001). Among 122 lipid-rich lesions, 61.8% in the alirocumab arm and 41.8% in the placebo arm showed a less lipid-rich plaque phenotype at follow-up (p = 0.03). Among 63 lesions with thin-cap fibroatheroma at baseline, 30.8% in the alirocumab arm and 8.1% in the placebo arm showed a fibrous/fibrocalcific plaque phenotype at follow-up (p = 0.02). Interpretation: The results of this trial indicate that compared with placebo, administration of alirocumab 150 mg biweekly within 24 hours after PCI for AMI results in a greater reduction in plaque burden and plaque regression at 52 weeks in the nonculprit vessel. All patients were also on high-dose rosuvastatin. LDL-C levels were reduced by nearly 85% with alirocumab + rosuvastatin compared with 51% with rosuvastatin alone. Clinical events were low. Clinical events were low. About one-third of patients achieved so-called “triple regression” of plaque, and this was higher among patients on alirocumab and those with higher baseline lipid accumulation. Patients who achieved triple regression had better clinical outcomes compared with those who did not. Lesion analysis confirmed PAV regression and conversion of presumed high-risk plaque to more stable, less lipid-rich plaque, although this latter aspect needs to be further validated. These are important data and provide further data regarding the utility of PCSK9 monoclonal antibodies for secondary prevention in high-risk patients (such as those with AMI) as combination therapy with high-dose statin therapy. In the ODYSSEY OUTCOMES trial, a similar reduction in LDL-C was noted with alirocumab, with a significant reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events when initiated 1-12 months (median 2.6 months) after an ACS presentation. This trial suggests that earlier initiation of the medication could be considered in high-risk patients. References: Biccirè FG, Kakizaki R, Koskinas KC, et al. Nicholls Professor of Cardiology, Theme Leader, South Australian Health and Medical Research Institute, University of Adelaide, Adelaide, Australia MBBS, PhD Find this author on Google Scholar Find this author on PubMed Search for this author on this site Cleveland Clinic Journal of Medicine December 2017, 84 (12 suppl 4) e1-e5; DOI: https://doi.org/10.3949/ccjm.84.s4.01 Article Figures & Data Info & Metrics PDF ABSTRACT Statins therapy reduces atheroma in proportion to the reduction of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C). Proprotein convertase subtilisin–kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitors are a new class of injectable human monoclonal antibodies shown to lower LDL-C when added to statin therapy. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study, 968 patients with symptomatic coronary artery disease were treated with statins alone or combined with the PCSK9 inhibitor, evolocumab, and assessed for change in percent, total volume, and regression of coronary atheroma. Treatment with statins plus evolocumab achieved mean LDL-C levels of 36.6 mg/dL, produced atheroma regression with a mean change in percent of atheroma volume of about 1% ( P < .001), and induced regression in a greater percentage of patients. The clinical benefits of LDL-C as low as 20 mg/dL shown in this trial warrant further investigation. KEY POINTS Statin therapy achieves regression of atherosclerosis in proportion to reductions in LDL-C. PCSK9 inhibitors are a new class of injectable human monoclonal antibodies shown to lower LDL-C when added to statin therapy. Treatment with statins plus the PCSK9 inhibitor, evolocumab, achieved mean LDL-C levels of 36.6 mg/dL, atheroma regression, and demonstrated clinical benefit for LDL-C as low as 20 mg/dL. Intravascular ultrasonography (IVUS) has been used for the past 20 years to measure atheromatous plaque in patients with coronary artery disease. The total volume of atherosclerosis in a coronary artery segment can be calculated using IVUS. A rotating transducer produces an image of a single, cross-sectional slice of the artery from which the atheroma area is calculated. A motorized device is used to withdraw the catheter, obtaining a series of cross-sectional slices at 1-mm intervals. The atheroma area for each slice is summated to obtain the total volume of atherosclerosis in the artery. IVUS has demonstrated that statins slow the progression or even induce regression of coronary atherosclerosis in proportion to the degree of reduction in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C). 1 – 4 No LDL-C-lowering therapy other than statins has shown regression of atherosclerosis in a trial using IVUS. The lowest LDL-C achieved in prior trials using statins was about 60 mg/dL. 1 , 3 While this is very low, lower levels have not previously been explored. Proprotein convertase subtilisin–kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitors, a new class of drugs, are injectable, fully human monoclonal antibodies that inactivate the PCSK9 protein. PCSK9 inhibitors have been shown to lower LDL-C incrementally when added to statins, achieving very low LDL-C levels. 5 , 6 However, no data exist describing the effect of low LDL-C levels reached using PCSK9 inhibitors on the progression of atherosclerosis. THE GLAGOV TRIAL The Global Assessment of Plaque Regression With a PCSK9 Antibody as Measured by Intravascular Ultrasound (GLAGOV) trial assessed the effect of PCSK9 inhibitor therapy on coronary atheroma. 7 The primary end point was the change in percent atheroma volume (PAV) after treatment, and secondary end points were the change in total atheroma volume and percent of patients with atheroma regression. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study included 968 patients with symptomatic coronary artery disease and other high-risk features from 197 centers around the world. Patients had a coronary angiogram with a vessel that contained an intermediate stenosis and received statin therapy for at least 4 weeks and had LDL-C levels greater than 80 mg/dL or 60 to 80 mg/dL with additional high-risk features. Following IVUS, patients were randomized for 18 months of treatment with either a statin alone or a statin plus a monthly injection of the PCSK9 inhibitor evolocumab. At the end of treatment, IVUS was performed in the same artery that we imaged at the beginning of the study ( Figure 1 ). The average age of patients was 60 and almost all were on statin therapy, with most taking high levels of high-intensity statins. Baseline LDL-C was very good at 92 mg/dL to 93 mg/dL, a level that would be considered good control by contemporary standards. To our knowledge, these are the lowest LDL-C levels that have ever been achieved in a major trial at the time. Starting at an LDL-C of 110 mg/dL to 20 mg/dL, there was a linear relationship between lower LDL-C and less atheroma progression ( Figure 4 ). This striking relationship was a uniform benefit across the full population and held for virtually every subgroup including by age, sex, baseline non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, diabetes presence or absence, and intensity of statin therapy. Total atheroma volume and percent of patients with atheroma regression The secondary end point measuring the total atheroma volume in the coronaries showed no change in total volume of atherosclerotic plaque in the statin monotherapy group and a decrease in the statin plus evolocumab group. An additional secondary end point was the percent of patients with atheroma regression, defined as any decrease in total atheroma volume or PAV. The percent of patients with total atheroma volume regression was greater in the statin plus evolocumab group (61.5%) than in the monotherapy group (48.9%; P < .001). PAV regression was also greater in patients in the statin plus evolocumab group (64%) compared with patients in the statin monotherapy group (47%; P < .001) ( Figure 5 ). It is important to note that atheroma regression cannot occur in all patients, as other factors drive atherosclerotic disease, but the high percentage of patients with manifest coronary disease experiencing regression in this study is encouraging. While this study was too small to evaluate morbidity and mortality, the rates of death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, hospitalization for unstable angina, and coronary vascularization trended in a favorable direction ( Table 2 ). analysis_trace: Trial NCT06896708 is a randomized controlled trial comparing intensive lipid-lowering therapy (LDL-C <1.0 mmol/L) versus standard therapy (LDL-C <1.8 mmol/L) in young/middle-aged patients (18-60 years) with chronic coronary syndrome. Primary endpoint is a composite of plaque progression (PAV increase >1%), MACE, death, or revascularization at 12 months.

Evidence from GLAGOV trial (Nissen et al., 2017): statin + evolocumab achieved LDL-C 36.6 mg/dL (~0.95 mmol/L) with mean PAV change of -0.95% (regression) vs no change with statin alone. 64% of patients achieved PAV regression with intensive therapy vs 47% with standard.

Evidence from PACMAN-AMI trial (Räber et al., 2022/2024): alirocumab + high-dose rosuvastatin achieved mean PAV change of -2.13% vs -0.92% with placebo + statin at 52 weeks. 84.6% vs 65.9% achieved PAV regression. LDL-C reduced by 85% vs 51%.

Evidence from SATURN trial (Nicholls et al., 2011): maximal dose rosuvastatin and atorvastatin both achieved significant plaque regression over 24 months, with rosuvastatin showing greater regression than atorvastatin (P=0.01).

Key differences from current trial: GLAGOV and PACMAN-AMI used IVUS imaging; current trial uses CCTA. GLAGOV was 18 months; current trial is 12 months. PACMAN-AMI was in AMI patients; current trial is chronic coronary syndrome. However, mechanism of plaque regression with intensive LDL lowering is well-established.
CCTA PAV measurement has demonstrated reproducibility for plaque monitoring per published literature (2020-2026). The 1% PAV progression threshold is clinically accepted.

For primary composite endpoint: Based on GLAGOV and PACMAN-AMI, intensive therapy shows ~15-20% absolute increase in plaque regression rates. MACE component expected to be low in this stable population over 12 months. Predict intensive group shows significantly lower composite event rate.

For secondary endpoints: PAV change (secondary-1, secondary-3, secondary-5) predicted to show greater regression in intensive group (-0.8% to -1.5% vs -0.2% to -0.5%). Non-calcified plaque (secondary-6) and high-risk plaques (secondary-7) expected to show greater reduction with intensive therapy based on PACMAN-AMI lesion-level analysis.

Agatston score (secondary-2) and CT-FFR (secondary-8) changes expected to favor intensive group but with smaller magnitude than PAV. FAI (secondary-9) may show modest change. Lesion reversal (secondary-4) expected to be higher in intensive group.
Safety: Both regimens use established drugs (atorvastatin/rosuvastatin, ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitors) with well-characterized safety profiles. No new safety signals anticipated.

Key uncertainty: 12-month duration is shorter than GLAGOV (18 months) and SATURN (24 months), potentially limiting magnitude of observable regression. CCTA vs IVUS measurement differences. Younger population may have different plaque characteristics.

Evidence gaps: No direct CCTA-based trials with this specific endpoint definition identified. No completed trials in exclusively young/middle-aged chronic coronary syndrome population. Trial is ongoing with expected completion 2027.
